insight.title: Why Train Tracks Are This Specific Width
insight.subtitle: The standard spacing of modern railway tracks was decided by the backside of Roman war horses.
insight.notificationHook: Train tracks are this wide for a reason

sections.text: Every major railway in America and Europe uses a highly specific standard track width of four feet, 8.5 inches. This arbitrary number was actually determined by the wheels of ancient Roman war chariots.

Roman empire roads were carved with deep ruts by heavy imperial chariots. To prevent their wagons from breaking, later European carriage makers spaced their wheels exactly to fit those ancient, pre-existing stone grooves.

When English engineers built the first steam railroads, they used those same carriage tools. Early immigrants brought this measurement to America, cementing a Roman imperial design into our modern high-speed transit networks.
Even our space rockets were shaped by Roman horses.
